newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says imports help keep lid on U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Buba says imports help keep lid on U.S. inflation.

text.p: The Bundesbank said in a report released on Thursday that growing imports into the U.S. should help keep U.S. price pressures weak.

The bank also said that U.S. second-quarter GDP growth of just over one percent from the previous quarter exaggerated the basic economic trend because the first quarter had been hit by production stoppages due to strikes in the auto industry and exceptionally bad weather.

This was particularly evident in the construction sector, where second-quarter home building investment was significantly higher than in the first three months, the Bundesbank said. But it added that the rise also reflected buoyant demand for residential accommodation.
Consumer demand was stimulating the economy although retail sales at mid-year indicated weakening demand, particularly for durable goods, the Bundesbank said.
Meanwhile trade was acting as a brake on economic output. While real exports had risen since the beginning of the year, imports had grown at an even stronger pace, the Bundesbank said.
"Growing supply from abroad should contribute to keeping price pressure weak," the Bundesbank said.
Producer prices in the June/July period were up just 0.5 percent year-on-year while consumer price inflation was about three percent.

"This is surprising in view of the tense situation on the labour market in most parts of the country and the fact that industrial capacity utilisation is running at above-average strength," the Bundesbank said.
